canonical_statement: EXTRACT-PE prospectively evaluated the safety and efficacy of the Indigo aspiration system without thrombolytic drugs for treatment of submassive acute pulmonary embolism.
EXTRACT-PE was a prospective, single-arm, multicenter investigational device exemption trial conducted at 22 U.S. sites.
Eligible patients were adults with symptoms of acute pulmonary embolism for 14 days or less, CTA-confirmed PE, systolic blood pressure at least 90 mm Hg, and RV/LV ratio greater than 0.9.

inclusion_criteria: Acute PE symptoms <=14 days with CTA evidence of PE
Systolic BP >=90 mm Hg with RV/LV ratio >0.9

canonical_statement: The supplement excluded patients with recent tPA, hemodynamic instability requiring support, severe/chronic pulmonary hypertension, high oxygen requirements, selected hematologic/renal/coagulation abnormalities, HIT or anticoagulation contraindication, recent major trauma or cardiopulmonary surgery, active chemotherapy, pregnancy, intracardiac thrombus, ECMO, short life expectancy, or concurrent investigational-study participation.

population.label: EXTRACT-PE eligibility population
exclusion_criteria: tPA within 14 days before baseline CTA
Systolic BP <90 mm Hg for 15 min or inotropic support
Peak PA pressure >70 mm Hg or severe/chronic pulmonary hypertension
FiO2 >40% or >6 L/min to maintain saturation >90%
Cardiovascular or pulmonary surgery within 7 days

canonical_statement: The Indigo aspiration system consisted of an 8-F aspiration catheter with tubing, pump, and separator; sustained aspiration was applied after advancing the catheter proximal to pulmonary arterial thrombus.

exposures.details: 8-F Indigo aspiration catheter with associated tubing, aspiration pump, and separator

canonical_statement: A centralized imaging core laboratory independently measured CTA RV/LV ratios and CT obstruction index, and baseline and 48-hour diameter measurements were separated in time to reduce potential bias.

A Clinical Events Committee adjudicated reported adverse events and superseded site assessments for final safety analyses, while an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board reviewed aggregate safety data.

The primary efficacy endpoint was the change in RV/LV diameter ratio from baseline to 48 hours; success required the lower bound of the two-sided 95% confidence interval for mean change to exceed 0.2.

The primary safety endpoint was the 48-hour rate of major adverse events, defined as device-related death, major bleeding, or device-related serious adverse events comprising clinical deterioration, pulmonary vascular injury, or cardiac injury; success required the upper 95% confidence bound to be below 40%.

outcome.definition: Composite of device-related death, major bleeding, or device-related serious adverse events

canonical_statement: All efficacy and safety outcomes were analyzed in the intention-to-treat population, defined as all patients who signed informed consent and were enrolled.
The modified intention-to-treat population excluded participants who received adjunctive clot-reduction treatments or thrombolytics during the procedure or through 48 hours after the procedure.

The supplement planned enrollment of up to 150 patients to provide 100 evaluable Indigo-treated patients, using assumptions of mean RV/LV change 0.42 (SD 0.36) and a 15% 48-hour major adverse event rate.
Between November 2017 and March 2019, EXTRACT-PE enrolled 119 patients at 22 U.S. investigational sites.
At enrollment, 118 of 119 patients had submassive pulmonary embolism and 1 had massive pulmonary embolism.
The mean baseline RV/LV ratio in the ITT population was 1.47 (SD 0.30; 95% CI 1.42 to 1.52).

canonical_statement: The study lacked randomization and a comparator arm and had no follow-up beyond 30 days.
The primary efficacy endpoint was the surrogate endpoint RV/LV ratio rather than a patient-centered clinical outcome.
The study was neither designed nor powered to assess long-term outcomes such as death, clinical deterioration, recurrent venous thromboembolism, exercise capacity, or quality of life.
The results cannot be generalized to higher-risk pulmonary embolism because the treated population was predominantly submassive PE.
Duration of device deployment and the decision to stop aspiration were left to operator discretion because the amount of thrombectomy could not be standardized.
The EXTRACT-PE trial was funded by Penumbra.
Several investigators reported financial relationships with Penumbra, including research support, speaking, consulting, and stock ownership; other industry relationships were also disclosed.

The authors concluded that the Indigo aspiration system met the trial's predefined safety and efficacy endpoints for acute PE and may be considered by endovascular physicians for intermediate-risk PE, while future prospective and randomized studies should identify which patients derive the greatest benefit.
